name: Hydroxychloroquine Sulphate
sections: 335.88 g/mol (base); 433.95 g/mol (sulfate; 200 mg sulfate ≈ 155 mg base)
White or almost white crystalline powder (sulfate), freely soluble in water.

Developed as a less toxic analogue of chloroquine; on the WHO List of Essential Medicines and a cornerstone of lupus therapy. First approval/introduction: US approval 1955 (Sterling Drug; patent filed 1949).

Accumulates in lysosomes raising intralysosomal pH, impairing antigen processing and MHC class II presentation; inhibits toll-like receptor (TLR7/9) signalling and cytokine production (IL-1, IL-6, TNF). Receptor / target profile: Raises lysosomal pH in antigen-presenting cells, inhibits TLR7/TLR9 signalling and haemozoin biocrystallisation (antimalarial).
Summary: Bioavailability ~74%; Tmax 2–4.5 h. Extensive tissue distribution (melanin-containing tissues). Partly metabolised (CYP2D6, 3A4). Terminal half-life ~40–50 days.
